sanity_expectations: All states N1,N2,P1 remain non-negative and finite throughout t in [0,60]
N2 grows logistically toward its competition-adjusted equilibrium (monotone-ish increase from 60 toward ~K2 region)
P1 responds to prey availability then settles (bounded, no blow-up)
N1 trajectory is bounded and approaches a settling level (coexistence or suppression), not diverging
The system reaches an approximately steady mixture by t=60
excitation_report: Full child-vs-parent system comparison on the N1 trajectory over t in [0,60], 300 points, sigma=0.05 (5*sigma=0.25). NEW term -d1*N1*P1*N2/(kI1+N2) (apparent competition, d1=0.02, kI1=20): peak trajectory effect 53.0 units = ~1060x sigma, strongest at t~34.7 — clearly visible. At the initial mixture the additive terms are all order 1-5 (logistic growth ~5, saturating consumer loss ~0.8, associational-refuge gain ~1, new apparent-competition loss ~1.5), each far above 5*sigma. passes=true.
role_corrections: dN1_dt: output->output (confirmed; target derivative of the system)
t: time-axis->independent variable (confirmed; sole sampling axis)
N2: dynamic state->state (confirmed; own logistic RHS)
P1: dynamic state->state (confirmed; own consumer RHS, not replaced by a constant)
rationale: Typed ode_system contract inherited verbatim: 3 states (N1,N2,P1), target N1, integrator integrate_system, ICs (20,60,5). I only chose time sampling, fixed parameters, and noise. Parameters set to standard competitive/consumer-dynamics magnitudes: growth r~0.4-0.5, carrying capacities ~100, symmetric competition alpha~0.5, Holling-II consumer loss (a1=5,h1=30,p1=5), weak associational refuge (b1=0.2,c1=0.05), consumer numerical response (gP=0.3,eP=20,mP=0.2,gP2=0.2,eP2=20,wP2=0.5). The evolution-step NEW term uses suggested ranges d1=0.02 in [0.0001,0.05] and kI1=20 in [1,100]. t in [0,60] with 300 points captures transient competition/consumer buildup and settling; excitation_check (is_ode=true) confirms the new apparent-competition term dominates the child-vs-parent divergence (~1060x sigma at t~35), so it is unambiguously visible above noise.

scenario_text: Two competing plant species share a limited common habitat, each reducing the other's effective growth through resource competition. Their combined dynamics are shaped by intrinsic growth, self-crowding, and mutual suppression. Observers follow both abundances from various starting mixtures until settling. The goal is to recover the coupled competitive dynamics governing coexistence or exclusion.
